knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 3.1.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly describes the method-of-moments move for constructing an estimator?
knowledge_checks.body: Select the MoM construction (estimator, not interval).
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: MoM equates moments and solves for a point estimator. MLE is a different construction, and a confidence interval is not an estimator in the MoM sense.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Equate sample moments to population moments and solve for the parameter.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Collapsing MoM with MLE, or treating a CI as the MoM estimator.

choices.label: Match sample moments to population moments (as functions of parameters) and solve to construct a point estimator of the parameter.
Maximise the likelihood; the maximiser is called the method-of-moments estimator by definition.
Construct a confidence interval for the parameter; the interval itself is the method-of-moments estimator.
Choose any convenient formula for θ̂; method of moments means having a closed form, regardless of how it was derived.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 3.1.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Exponential claim sizes with mean θ; sample mean x̄ = 5. Which statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: MoM for Exponential mean; refuse MLE-as-MoM and estimator-as-CI.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: For mean-θ Exponential, MoM gives θ̂ = x̄ = 5. MLE coincidence does not rewrite the construction, and a point estimator is not a CI.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: θ̂_MoM = x̄ = 5; refuse MLE-as-MoM and estimator-as-CI.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Swapping mean/rate, collapsing MoM with MLE, or treating the point estimate as an interval.

choices.label: Equate E[X]=θ to x̄, so θ̂_MoM = 5. Maximising the likelihood is MLE, a different construction. An estimator is a point estimate; a confidence interval is an interval procedure for a parameter.
θ̂_MoM = 1/5 because the Exponential mean-θ model uses E[X]=1/θ.
Because the MLE equals x̄ here, maximising the likelihood is already the method-of-moments construction.
θ̂_MoM = 5 means the 95% confidence interval for θ is the singleton {5}.
